Offline • No account • No tracking New: flatness & circularity from dial readings

Flatness and circularity — without the spreadsheet walk.

The traditional workflow is familiar: write down the dial readings, walk back to the office PC, open the Excel macro, run Solver, copy the numbers into a report. CNC Workpiece Calculator 1.0.2 puts that whole loop in your pocket — a minimum-zone flatness solver and a three-way circularity fitter that run on-device in under a second, next to the probe centering, ISO fits, tolerances and weight tools the app already had.

Geometry NEW IN 1.0.2

Flatness and circularity are where inspection gets painful. The measurement itself takes two minutes with a dial indicator — the math is what kills the job: a minimum Z-band problem that nobody solves by hand, usually delegated to an Excel macro with Solver that lives on one PC, guarded by file locks and macros-enabled warnings.

Three circle fits, honestly labeled

Algebraic least-squares, geometric best-fit and a Nelder–Mead minimum-zone search run together. The Excel-compatible diameter difference and the tighter minimum-zone radial range are reported separately — no more arguing between old and new conventions.

Six chart views

Layout, deviation ×10, residual, 3D plane, contour and center zoom — switch live as the points come in. Selected points are highlighted, and the view scales itself to your data.

Export that fits the workflow

One tap renders a 1200×800 PNG with the chart and a results panel, straight to Photos or the share sheet. Points export as CSV. Saved sessions reload later from the More panel.

Everything else it does

The Geometry tab joins the tools the app already shipped with — all offline, all on-device.

Probe-based centering

Enter measured X/Y points (with probe diameter compensation) and calculate the center/geometry for circle, rectangle, ellipse, straight slot, and double-circle patterns.

Shaft–hole fits

Quickly check nominal size + tolerance grades (e.g., H7/h6) and see fit outcomes while selecting common hole/shaft types.

General tolerances

Reference size and geometric tolerances (straightness/flatness, perpendicularity, circular runout, etc.) with clear results for shop use.

Weight estimation

Estimate weight for common shapes (plate, tube, bar, ring…) with material presets, quantity, and metric/imperial units.

Built for gloved hands

A custom numeric keypad with first-tap replace, sign toggle and auto-scroll — no fighting the stock keyboard mid-measurement.

Offline & private

No account, no ads, no tracking SDKs. Sessions save on-device. It works in restricted shop networks because it never needs a network at all.

FAQ

Can it replace my Excel flatness macro with Solver?

For shop-floor use, yes — the Geometry tab solves the same minimum Z-band problem with a two-phase simplex LP solver, on device, in under a second. It reports the flatness value, the initial range, the leveling reduction, the fitted plane and per-point leveling advice. For audit-grade documentation you can export the points as CSV and process them in your own tools.

Which circularity number does it report — the old diameter difference or the minimum zone?

Both, kept separate on purpose: the diameter difference at the algebraic center (the classic workbook convention) and the minimum-zone radial range (the tighter, standard-conforming value).

How do I enter indicator readings for circularity?

Switch to Indicator mode, enter the diameter where the indicator reads zero as the Ø Datum, then enter each signed reading. The dial sign setting matches how your indicator is mounted (needle up = larger or smaller radius).

What is the leveling advice based on?

The fitted minimum-band plane. For each measured point it shows the suggested rigid-body correction and the predicted residual after correction — the improvement you can expect from shimming or re-leveling alone, before any machining.

Can I export results for my quality records?

Yes. One tap renders a 1200×800 PNG containing the chart and a highlighted results panel, saved to Photos or the share sheet. The measured points export as CSV for further processing.

Does the app need an internet connection?

No. All calculations, charts, saved sessions and exports work offline.

Does it collect any data?

No developer analytics or tracking SDKs are used. See the full policy on the Privacy page.

Can I use it on iPad?

Yes — the UI is built for both iPhone and iPad workflows.

Where do I report a bug or request a feature?

Email wangning.engineer@outlook.com.
